deviations.claim_in_article: “A call seemed to come from an AI agent. But as the conversation went on, the voice was not AI at all. It was a person. Meta had run a test that caused exactly this surprise.”
deviations.issue: The article presents a recipient discovering during a call that a person, not AI, was speaking, and says the test caused this surprise. The Ledger verifies that trained contract workers made some Muse calls, but does not establish that recipients experienced this reveal.
deviations.explanation: The English version turns the source’s suggestive framing into an asserted event and adds an unverified recipient reaction. This is a changed fact, strengthened certainty, and unsupported new claim.
deviations.qualifier_text: “seemed to come from an AI agent”

deviations.claim_in_article: 見出しと冒頭では、電話の相手がAIだと思って会話を続けた後、実は人間だと分かった具体的な出来事として描いている。
「Meta had run a test that caused exactly this surprise」と、テストが相手の驚きを引き起こしたと述べている。
テストが「ユーザーに、契約スタッフが電話をかけることを明確に伝えないまま」始まったとし、ユーザーが相手をAIだと思った可能性も述べている。本文後半でも同じく、ユーザーに明確に伝えずに始めたとしている。
“They enjoyed the ease of AI. But they did not know that a human was on the other end.”
deviations.issue: 記事は利用者が実際にAIの利便性を享受し、人間が電話していると知らなかったと断定しているが、Ledgerが確認するのは適切な開示なしにテストが始まったことまでで、利用者の認識や反応は確認していない。原文の条件付き・比喩的な表現を、翻訳で実際に起きた事実のように強めている。
deviations.explanation: Ledgerにない利用者の反応・認識を事実として追加し、原文の留保を弱めているため。
deviations.qualifier_text: 直前の文に “If this was not explained clearly” という条件があるが、対象の2文では利用者の反応・認識を断定している。

deviations.claim_in_article: They enjoyed the ease of AI.
But they did not know that a human was on the other end.
It said that human staff made inappropriate comments about race during calls to bargain over internet or cable fees.
The fee plan left the stage, but the events driving oil prices—and the prices themselves—quickly returned.
deviations.issue: The sentence describes the events as having quickly returned and as driving oil prices, whereas HF-009 reports that relevant attacks, blockade and tanker-safety concerns continued during the price movement. It changes continued events into returning events and asserts a causal role not established by the Ledger.
deviations.explanation: The timing changes from concerns that continued to events that returned, and the sentence adds an unsupported causal link between those events and oil prices.

deviations.claim_in_article: “Normally, removing the fee plan would seem likely to calm oil prices.”
“The fee plan left the stage, but the events driving oil prices—and the prices themselves—quickly returned.”
“Even so, trends now look different. Bags no longer play a game with only one size on the throne.”
“Concerns about US-Iran attacks, the sea blockade, and tanker safety continued on July 14. So the flashy 20% plan left the stage.”
deviations.issue: The word “So” implies that the continuing concerns caused the 20% plan to be withdrawn. The Ledger does not establish that causal link; it records Trump’s explanation that the replacement decision followed discussions with Middle Eastern leaders.
deviations.explanation: “So” turns the juxtaposition into a causal claim not supported by the Ledger. This is a new factual relationship as well as a changed causality and unsupported new claim.
